stem.text: Compound X, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{13}\text{Br}$, reacts with hot alcoholic $\text{NaOH}$ to produce two compounds, Y and Z.
On reaction with $\text{Br}_2$, Y gives a product, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{Br}_2$, which exists as a mixture of four optical isomers.
On reaction with $\text{Br}_2$, Z gives a product, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{Br}_2$, which is non-chiral.

A.alt: Cyclohexane ring with CH3 and Br both attached to the same ring carbon (1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane).

B.alt: Cyclohexane ring with a CH2Br group attached to one ring carbon (bromomethylcyclohexane).

C.alt: Cyclohexane ring with CH3 and Br on adjacent ring carbons (1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane).

D.alt: Cyclohexane ring with CH3 and Br on ring carbons 1 and 3 (1-bromo-3-methylcyclohexane).
